title: Immigrants from Ukraine and Sudan to keep deportation protections for now
content: Immigrants from Ukraine and Sudan are expected to be allowed to continue to live and work in the United States for now after their deportation protections were set to expire this week, the Department of Homeland Security said. Temporary Protected Status is a form of humanitarian relief that provides people fleeing war, natural disasters or humanitarian crises with temporary permission to remain in the US without fear of being deported. As of March 2025, there were more than 100,000 Ukrainians and more than 1,790 nationals of Sudan enrolled in the program, according to federal data . TPS protections for both countries were slated to end Monday. A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said in statement to CNN that announcements on TPS for Ukraine and Sudan “will be made at the appropriate time.” Until those announcements are made, immigrants from Ukraine and Sudan who are in the US retain protections, the spokesperson said. The Trump administration, which has terminated TPS for multiple countries in its efforts to curb immigration, took a similar approach for nationals of El Salvador earlier this year, allowing them to keep protections pending an announcement. Trump administration officials have repeatedly argued that the permissions are temporary and not a permanent solution, criticizing previous administrations for repeatedly extending them. The US Supreme Court in June allowed the Trump administration to end temporary deportation protections for hundreds of thousands of foreign nationals from Haiti and Syria who have endured war and natural disasters. Those who have lost TPS status have faced fear and confusion because they are vulnerable to detention and deportation at any time. And Salvadorans who spoke with CNN last month said they’re increasingly concerned their days in the US could be numbered.
ranking_reason: TPS protections for Ukrainian and Sudanese immigrants have been extended, allowing them to continue living and working in the US without fear of deportation.

analysis.reason: TPS protections for Ukrainian and Sudanese immigrants have been extended, allowing them to continue living and working in the US without fear of deportation.

final_quality.reason: The article reports a substantive, important development in the category of people, specifically immigration, providing a clear reason for readers to care. The extension of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Ukrainian and Sudanese immigrants affects over 100,000 individuals and provides humanitarian relief, making it a newsworthy story.

title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff survives shooting attempt in Mumbai
content:
Police in India's Mumbai city are investigating a shooting attempt on Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff, who survived without sustaining any gunshot wounds.
The 36-year-old was shot at on Sunday evening while he was in a car leaving a football ground in Juhu suburb. Videos showed at least two men firing multiple shots at close range at the front passenger seat of Shroff's car while it was moving slowly past a crowd.
Two people, including Shroff's driver, were injured, according to the police. Reports say three men have been detained in connection with the incident.
The attack has sent shockwaves through Bollywood, with celebrities raising concerns about Shroff's safety.
Several actors and political figures in Mumbai have been targeted by gunmen in recent years.
Shroff, the son of veteran Bollywood actor Jackie Shroff, made his film debut with Heropanti in 2014. He has appeared in many action films, and is popular with fans for his dancing and martial arts skills.
He is also a professional footballer and made his debut for Mumbay FC in October 2024 in a regional tournament. He was leaving the football ground after his regular practice session when the attack happened
Eknath Shinde, deputy chief minister of Maharashtra state of which Mumbai is the capital, visited Shroff after the shooting on Sunday evening, and said the actor had been left "shaken" by the attack.
"These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated, and we will put an end to this hooliganism," Shinde said.
In a photograph showing Shroff with Shinde, the actor is seen shirtless with some bandages on his upper body. It's not clear yet what injuries he sustained.
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis described the incident as "serious and condemnable", and said that the police would arrest some people "very soon".
He said he had told Shroff that he should not worry, and that the government would ensure his "complete safety".
The All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA), a large union, condemned the attack, alleging that gangsters were deliberately targeting people in the film industry to create an "atmosphere of fear" and extort money from celebrities.
In a statement, the association criticised the government and police for failing to prevent such attacks. It called for strict action against those responsible and better security for film industry workers and their families.
The association also said the incident was a reminder of the 1990s, when criminal gangs wielded considerable influence in the city. It said that the film industry should not have to "work under the shadow of fear".
Police have not yet confirmed who was behind the shooting. But Indian media reports have been widely reporting that an audio clip has surfaced in which a man claiming to be linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang says he is responsible.
Bishnoi is currently lodged in a high-security prison in Gujarat state in connection with several high-profile cases.
The authenticity of the recording and the man's claims have not been independently verified and police have not confirmed the gang's involvement yet.
But the reports have brought the Bishnoi gang back into the headlines.
In 2024, police arrested two people allegedly linked to the Bishnoi gang for a gun attack that targeted the home of Bollywood superstar Salman Khan.
ranking_reason: Attempted shooting of Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff, a notable celebrity in the entertainment industry.

analysis.reason: Attempted shooting of Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff, a notable celebrity in the entertainment industry.

final_quality.reason: This article reports a substantive and potentially significant development in the entertainment industry, with the attempted shooting of a well-known Bollywood actor. The fact that the actor survived and that the attack has sent shockwaves through the industry suggests a potential impact on the community and the industry as a whole.

title: Australian Greens senator denies claims of misconduct towards women
content:
An Australian Greens senator has denied allegations of inappropriate behaviour towards women and accused his party of "nasty political games", days after the claims emerged.
Last Thursday, Greens leader David Shoebridge said Senator Jordon Steele-John, 32, had taken leave from the party room after a letter from seven current and former members said he had been accused of "multiple allegations" of misconduct between 2017 and 2025.
In an online post on Sunday, the senator denied the claims and said he was not on leave. On a sexual assault claim, he said police investigating the matter had closed the case and no charges were laid.
An internal party probe has been launched into the allegations.
Steele-John, who has cerebral palsy and uses a wheelchair, was first elected to the senate in Western Australia in November 2017.
In his letter responding to the claims, Steele-John said his nickname - "Feels on wheels" - initially referred to him being emotional when advocating for disability rights but had since taken on a "more sinister meaning" about his alleged mistreatment of women.
He accused Shoebridge of mishandling the matter and questioned the timing of the letter, saying "it is no coincidence" that the allegations were sent to the leader "the day after we agreed on the timeline for the next preselection" ahead of the next federal election.
Days after the letter with the claims was sent to Shoebridge, local media reported that the party had created a 47-page dossier years earlier that listed a number of allegations against Steele-John and how to manage media coverage if they emerged.
Steele-John said the dossier was made so that the media would not "bombard" the two women at the centre of those claims and that neither woman had made a complaint.
He acknowledged the allegations against him would have "damaged" the public's trust in him and said he was "committed to rebuilding that by acting with as much transparency and accountability as I can".
Shoebridge's office confirmed that the allegations had been referred to the Independent Parliamentary Standards Commission.
A spokesperson for Shoebridge said the leader still believed "leave is appropriate under the circumstances" and taking leave would not influence the internal party investigation.
ranking_reason: Accusations of misconduct against an Australian Greens senator, with a political leader's response and an internal party probe launched.

analysis.reason: Accusations of misconduct against an Australian Greens senator, with a political leader's response and an internal party probe launched.

final_quality.reason: The article reports a substantively important development in the category of people, specifically in Australian politics, with allegations of misconduct against a senator and the subsequent denial and response from the party leader. The article provides a clear reason for readers to care, as it highlights the impact of such allegations on the public's trust in political leaders and the party's internal processes.
